title: The Reckoning
objective: Decide what Ashenveld becomes, and whether you stay.

default: It is three days since the ritual.

default.text: The curse is still in Ashenveld. It is spreading more slowly, but it is spreading. The turns come less often, though they have not stopped. The grey at Issa's fingertips has not gone back.
default.else: The curse is still in Ashenveld. It was never going to vanish in three days. But it has stopped spreading. Crestfall feels quite different. People who were having the turns have them less often now, and they don't last so long. The grey at Issa's fingertips has not gone, but it has gone no further.

default: The powers in the town are gathering themselves again. It always comes after anything big: working out what it meant, and who should have the credit, and what happens next.

default.text: Seriva's bargain is already being kept. The grey flag has come down from the alderman's hall.

default: Vorne has his view of it, and Seriva has hers, and the Rootless camp has its own. And you have to decide what becomes of Ashenveld, and of you in it.
text.commander:
You sit at your usual table in the Tallow and consider the three parties drawn up round the question of what happens now.

Vorne wants the account of the ruins and a say in what becomes of them. Seriva wants the Covenant's part in the rebuilding formally recognised. The Rootless want recognition, and supplies, and to be left alone.

None of these need clash. But somebody will have to bring them together. You have done it before.
text.arcane:
Three days of watching have given you a first idea of what the seal has done.

The curse is not going back quickly. In people in the early stages, like Issa and Lira, it is going on more slowly. In those further gone you can see no change at all as yet.

It is the land that answers first. Birds are beginning to come back to the places nearest Crestfall. How long the rest will take is the question.
text.ranger:
You have been watching the land mend as you would watch any change in it, patiently, looking for the signs.

It is going the right way, and slowly. The deepest parts will take longest.

But this morning you heard a bird, in the ordinary trees half a mile out of Crestfall, of a kind you had not heard since you came back. You stood in the road and listened to it a good deal longer than you needed to.
text.cipher:
For three days you have been thinking of nothing but who will come out on top.

Whoever controls the account of what happened, and what it is taken to mean, will hold the power in Ashenveld for the next ten years.

The story is still being written, and you are one of the people writing it.

choices.text: Bring the three of them together, and work out a settlement that will last.

text: It takes most of a day to get them all into one room.
There is Vorne, and Maret, and Seriva, and Edric.
You go between them for three hours, and at last you find a way of putting it that gives each of them enough to agree to.

text.text: Vorne has the account, and the credit for the Compact keeping order. Seriva admits it in the room, in front of all of them: she broke the seal twenty years ago. Nobody lets the Covenant off anything. The Rootless camp is recognised, and has a share of the supplies. Edric keeps a small part as an adviser.
text.else: Vorne has the account, and the credit for the Compact keeping order. Seriva has the Covenant formally cleared, and the story becomes that the seal simply wore out with time, not that she damaged it. The Rootless camp is recognised, and has a share of the supplies. Edric keeps a small part as an adviser.

text: It is not justice. It is something the people in the room can live with, which is about as near to justice as any committee is likely to come.

success_at_cost.text:
You reach a settlement, but it is a fragile one. One of them has agreed to terms they mean to drop as soon as they safely can.

It is better than nothing, but you can already see where it will break.

failure.text:
The meeting comes to nothing. Vorne and Seriva cannot agree at all about how much the Covenant is to blame, and Maret won't accept any terms that make the camp answer to either of them.

You come away with three separate truces, and no peace.

choices.text: Side with the Rootless, and help Maret make the camp's future safe.

default.text:
You go to the camp and tell Maret what you mean to do.

She looks at you. "Why?"

You tell her. The Rootless were here before the Compact came. They looked after the afflicted when nobody else would. They know the land and they know the curse. Of everyone in Ashenveld they are the most capable of carrying on, and they have the least power.

"I'm going to help you get the account," you say. "And make sure the Compact recognises the camp before Vorne can think of a reason not to."

Maret is quiet. "That will make enemies," she says.

"I know," you say.

choices.text: Work with Vorne. Only the Compact can hold Ashenveld steady for the long run.

default.text:
You go to Vorne and tell him where you stand.

The Compact has money and reach, and it is not going anywhere. What Ashenveld needs now is rebuilding, and rebuilding needs the Compact to put its hand in its pocket.

For your support, the account and your evidence and what you know of Seriva's part, you want promises: help for the villages the curse touched, money for Crestfall to recover, and protection for the Rootless camp.

Vorne hears you out. "You drive a harder bargain than Cael," he says.

"Cael works for you," you say. "I don't."

choices.text: Ask Edric to keep the seal.
choices.locked_hint: Needs the Covenant, or Edric, on your side

default.text:
You find him at the shrine, among the candles. You ask him to keep the seal: to walk east every month and listen, and write down what he hears, and go on doing it after you have gone.

He is quiet a long while. "We were made to seal it," he says. "Not like this. But we were made to seal it." That afternoon he gives Pol all the purification texts, in a box tied up with string, and does not ask for them back.

text.default:
You and [missing person] have an evening to yourselves, the first real one since you found them in the outskirts.

It is at the Tallow. The fire is better tonight than it has been for weeks; Aldous is burning the good wood, the kind he keeps for occasions.

[missing person] sits across from you. They look different in the firelight than they did in the light of the chamber. Or perhaps you see them differently now. The mechanism read everything, including what you have felt about this person for eleven years and longer.

They went through the same reading. They know things now that they never chose to know.
text.commander:
"The mechanism showed me why you left," they say.

"Yes," you say.

"The real reason. Not the war. The one under the war."

"Yes," you say again.

"I knew some of it," they say. "I did not know the whole of it." They pause. "It does not change why I wrote the letter. It changes what it cost me to write it."
text.arcane:
"There is something I want to tell you," they say. "Something the mechanism showed me about myself that I did not know before."

They tell you.

It is not what you expected. It is about the fourteen months, not the ruins or the ritual, but what they came to understand about themselves while they were alone, and what being alone made plain.

You listen. They have never told anyone this.
text.ranger:
"What did it show you?" they ask. "About me."

You think how to answer honestly.

"That you came back to Ashenveld for the same reason you left," you say. "That it was one reason all along. You've been trying to sort something out about yourself for eleven years, and the ruins were the first place where it seemed it might be sorted."

They look at you a long while. "Yes," they say. "Does it change how you see me?"

"No," you say, and you mean it.
text.cipher:
"I know what you did not tell me," they say. "By the fire, before the ritual."

You look at them.

"You let the mechanism read it," they say. "You chose to let it read you rather than say it yourself. I want you to know that I understand why. And I know what it was."

Neither of you says anything for a while.

"Can we talk about it?" you ask.

"Yes," they say. "But not tonight."

"All right," you say.

choices.text: Be honest about what the mechanism showed you about them.

text: You tell them.
You don't tell them all of it. There is more than one evening's worth.

text.text: You tell them about the market days, and the docks, and the barges, a whole year of it.
You tell them about the warehouse door, and that you never knew they were standing in it.
You tell them about your mother asking for you, and what they told her.
You tell them about the lamp and the old texts, and that you know now why they sent you away.
You tell them about the pier, and how long they watched the barge, and what they felt while they watched.
You tell them about the mill wall, and that they knew, and that they waited.

text: They listen without interrupting. When you have finished they are quiet a long while.
"I did not know you knew that," they say at last.
"I didn't know it till the chamber," you say.
"Nor did I," they say. "I am glad we both know now."

choices.text: Keep some things back. Not everything needs saying tonight.

text: You keep some things back, and so do they. The mechanism read everything, but you are not the mechanism.
You both know, roughly, what the ritual showed you, and you leave it there between you without putting it all into words.
You sit by the fire and don't say everything, and it is a comfortable silence.
"Tonight I want to just be in this room with you," they say. "Without anything needing to be resolved."

text.default:
It is the morning of the sixteenth day.

You are sitting at your table in the Tallow when it becomes plain that today is the day things are settled. You have been making up your mind for days. Today is the day it becomes very hard to change it.

The others have taken their positions, and you have taken yours. [missing person] is here, and Pol, and Maret and Branch, and Lira and Issa, and Aldous behind his bar with the good wood still burning.

What matters now is not what you have done. It is what you will do next.
text.commander:
You have been working towards an end, and you know where you stand. What comes next is carrying it out, and in the state Ashenveld is in that may mean staying a long while. It may mean staying for good.

You think about what that would mean, and then you decide.
text.arcane:
There is an account to write: [missing person]'s fourteen months of notes, Pol's fifteen years of learning, and what you have seen yourself.

What matters is who is given it, and what it says happened. That will decide what Ashenveld becomes.
text.ranger:
Ashenveld needs time, and now it has time. But it also needs people who can read what is happening and know what to do about it.

You wonder whether you are one of those people, and what it would mean to stay.
text.cipher:
You can see how things stand. Whoever wants to keep a say here will have to stay, and keep on managing people, and keep watching who is doing what and why.

You have done it in other places, for other reasons. The question is whether you want to do it here.

choices.text: Stay in Ashenveld. The work is here.

text: You decide to stay.
Nobody is making you. You stay because the work is here, and you know what it is and how to do it.
You find [missing person] and tell them.
They look at you for a moment. "I was going to ask you," they say. "But I did not want to ask you to stay for me rather than for the place."
"You needn't have worried," you say.
They nod. "Then I am staying too."

text.text: "Somebody has to mend the east field fence," they say. "It was always going to be us."
They take your hand, as they did on the mill wall, and don't let go of it for some time.
"The house on the mill lane has new shutters," they say. "We will need our own."
"Good," they say. "There is a great deal you still do not know."
"Then I shall find out at last what you are like when you stay somewhere," they say.
"Good," they say, and look at you rather longer than the word needs.

choices.text: Leave Ashenveld with [missing person]. You came for them, and the rest is done.

text: You decide to go.
The curse is sealed, and the others have their arrangement. Ashenveld has begun to mend, and it doesn't need you here for that.
You came here for one reason, and the reason is standing in front of you.
You find [missing person] and tell them you are going.
Their face changes. It is not disappointment, quite. "I thought..." they begin, and stop. "All right," they say. "When?"

text.text: "You never did say whether you forgave me," they say.

text: "Now," you say. "Before something else needs mending."

text.text: "West, then," they say. "You go first. You always did."
"This time say goodbye to somebody," they say. "Anybody. Practise on Aldous."
"She would have liked to see us leave together," they say. "For once."
"I sent you away once," they say. "This time I am coming."
"I watched you go once," they say. "I am not doing that again."
"Then say it on the road," they say. "It is a long road."

choices.text: Send [missing person] on ahead. Stay long enough to finish what needs finishing, then follow.

text: "Go," you tell them. "Get somewhere safe and ordinary and rest. I'll follow."
They look at you as they have looked at you ever since the ruins. They have been reading you for longer than you have been reading them.
"You will," they say.
"Yes," you say.

text.text: At the door they say, "Write more than twice."
At the door they say, "Do not leave me standing in a doorway again."
At the door they say, "I will keep you a room. You are paying for it."
At the door they say, "Finish it properly. Then come and tell me how."
At the door they say, "I will be watching the road. I am good at it."
At the door they say, "I will wait. I am good at that too."

text: They go. You watch them leave the Tallow, cross the market square, and turn west on to the road that leads somewhere that is not Ashenveld.
You have a week's work left, or perhaps two. Then you will follow.

choices.text: Stay in Ashenveld alone. [missing person] has earned the right to leave, and you're not ready to.

text: You tell them to go without you.

It is not the easiest conversation you have ever had. But you tell them the truth: you have not finished here. Ashenveld has not finished with you, nor you with it, and you can't leave while that is so.
They look at you a long time.
"Will you come when it is done?" they ask.
"I don't know," you say. You owe them the truth more than you owe them comfort.

text.text: At the door they say, "You still owe me cider," and they don't look back.
At the door they stop, and you think they are going to say it. They don't, and neither do you.
At the door they say, "I will tell people you are on your way." It is what they told your mother.
At the door they say, "You were always going to be better at this than me." It doesn't sound like praise.
At the door they say, "I am proud of you," and they have gone before you can answer.
At the door they look back once, and then they have gone.

text: They nod, and go. The door of the Tallow shuts behind them.
You sit at your table. Aldous brings you something without being asked, and the fire burns.
Outside, Ashenveld is slowly beginning to remember how to be a place where people can live.
